rationales: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron, not the tendency to lose one.
Electropositivity is the tendency of an atom to lose valence electrons.
Valency is an atom’s combining capacity.
Hardness describes resistance to scratching or deformation.
Graphite is soft and slippery.
Phosphorus is generally soft or brittle.
Iodine is a brittle solid, not extremely hard.
Diamond is an extremely hard form of carbon.
H₂ is a diatomic molecule.
NH₃ contains four atoms, so it is not diatomic.
O₂ is a diatomic molecule.
HCl is a diatomic molecule.
An ionic bond forms through electrostatic attraction between ions.
A covalent bond involves shared electrons, but this is not the specific name for a dative bond.
A metallic bond involves attraction between metal ions and delocalized electrons.
A dative covalent bond is also called a coordinate covalent bond.
The O shell has five subshells.
The N shell has four subshells.
The L shell has two subshells.
The M shell has three subshells.
Mendeleev’s table was based primarily on atomic mass.
The long-form periodic table is arranged according to atomic number.
Atomic mass is not the basis of the modern long-form periodic table.
Valency is not the basis of the table’s construction.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of the halogens.
Chlorine is less electronegative than fluorine.
Bromine is less electronegative than chlorine and fluorine.
Iodine is the least electronegative among these halogens.
Sodium has one electron in its outermost shell.
Seven is not sodium’s number of valence electrons.
Eleven is sodium’s total number of electrons in a neutral atom.
Twenty-three is approximately sodium’s mass number, not its number of valence electrons.
Charles presented his law in 1787.
1662 is associated with the publication of Boyle’s law.
1913 is not the year Charles presented his law.
1932 is not the year Charles presented his law.
% m/m expresses the mass of solute per 100 g of solution.
% m/v expresses the mass of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
% v/m expresses the volume of solute per 100 g of solution.
% v/v expresses the volume of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
NaCl is a strong electrolyte because it dissociates extensively in water.
NaOH is a strong electrolyte because it dissociates extensively in water.
H₂SO₄ is generally classified as a strong electrolyte.
CH₃COOH is a weak electrolyte because it ionizes only partially in water.
Hydrogen has oxidation number −1 in metal hydrides.
Hydrogen is usually +1 in compounds with non-metals, but not in metal hydrides.
Hydrogen does not have oxidation number −2 in metal hydrides.
Hydrogen does not have oxidation number +2 in metal hydrides.
Phosphorus is not the standard example of a lustrous non-metal.
Graphite can have a sheen, but iodine is the usual textbook example of a lustrous non-metal.
Sulphur is generally described as a dull non-metal.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
6.02 × 10²³ atoms equals one mole of carbon atoms.
Half a mole contains about 3.01 × 10²³ atoms.
0.2 mole contains about 1.204 × 10²³ atoms.
0.1 mole contains about 6.02 × 10²² atoms.
Helium has two electrons, not the ten in sodium’s resulting configuration.
After losing one electron, sodium has the same electron configuration as neon.
Argon has eighteen electrons, more than sodium has after losing one electron.
Xenon has fifty-four electrons, far more than sodium has after losing one electron.
